en værtindegave.explanation: "En værtindegave" means "a hostess gift". It is built from "en værtinde" (a hostess) and "en gave" (a gift). The part "gave" is also in "en fødselsdagsgave" (a birthday present): "Jeg købte en fødselsdagsgave" (I bought a birthday present).

en væske.explanation: "En væske" means "a liquid". To tell someone to drink plenty, use it for the fluids you drink: "Drik meget væske" (Drink a lot of fluids).

et valg.explanation: "Et valg" means "a choice". To say a decision is up to someone: "Det er dit valg" (It is your choice). When you talk about voting for a parliament or a president, it means "an election": "Der er valg i år" (There is an election this year).

et vandfald.explanation: "Et vandfald" means "a waterfall". It is built from "vand" (water) and "et fald" (a fall). To talk about a drop in numbers, "et fald" is also used: "et fald i prisen" (a fall in the price).

et vandland.explanation: "Et vandland" means "a water park". It is built from "vand" (water) and "land" (land), so literally a land of water.

et vandrerhjem.explanation: "Et vandrerhjem" means "a hostel". It is built from "en vandrer" (a hiker) and "et hjem" (a home), so literally a hiker's home. The part "hjem" is also in "et plejehjem" (a nursing home): "Min farmor bor på plejehjem" (My grandmother lives in a nursing home).

et vareudvalg.explanation: "Et vareudvalg" means "a range of goods". It is built from "en vare" (an item) and "et udvalg" (a selection). The word "et udvalg" also means a committee: "Kommunen har nedsat et udvalg" (The municipality has set up a committee).

et varsel.explanation: "Et varsel" means "a notice / warning". To talk about a weather warning: "Der er et varsel om storm i aften" (There is a storm warning tonight). To talk about advance notice at work: "Fagforeningen har givet varsel om strejke" (The union has given notice of a strike).

et vaskemærke.explanation: "Et vaskemærke" means "a care label". It is built from "vaske" (wash) and "et mærke" (a label). The word "et mærke" also means a brand: "et kendt mærke" (a famous brand).

et vaskeri.explanation: "Et vaskeri" means "a laundromat". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and the ending "-eri", which names a place where the work is done, as in "et bageri" (a bakery): "Vi køber brød på bageriet" (We buy bread at the bakery).

et vaskerum.explanation: "Et vaskerum" means "a laundry room". It is built from "vaske" (wash) and "et rum" (a room). The part "rum" is also in "et gæsterum" (a guest room): "Du kan sove i gæsterummet" (You can sleep in the guest room).

et vejskilt.explanation: "Et vejskilt" means "a road sign". It is built from "en vej" (a road) and "et skilt" (a sign). The word "et skilt" also works for any sign with writing: "et skilt på døren" (a sign on the door).

et vendepunkt.explanation: "Et vendepunkt" means "a turning point". It is built from "at vende" (to turn) and "et punkt" (a point). To talk about a match, use it like this: "Det var et vendepunkt i kampen" (It was a turning point in the match).

et venskab.explanation: "Et venskab" means "a friendship". It is built from "en ven" (a friend) and the ending "-skab". The same ending is in "et fællesskab" (a community): "Vi har et godt fællesskab i klassen" (We have a good community in the class).

et venteværelse.explanation: "Et venteværelse" means "a waiting room". It is built from "at vente" (to wait) and "et værelse" (a room). The part "værelse" is also in "et soveværelse" (a bedroom): "Vi har to soveværelser" (We have two bedrooms).

et verdenshav.explanation: "Et verdenshav" means "an ocean". It is built from "en verden" (a world) and "et hav" (a sea). To say you swim in the sea: "Jeg bader i havet" (I swim in the sea).

et vers.explanation: "Et vers" means "a verse". When it means poetry in general, it has no article: "Han skriver vers" (He writes poetry).

et videoopkald.explanation: "Et videoopkald" means "a video call". It is built from "video" (video) and "et opkald" (a call). To talk about an ordinary phone call, use "et opkald" alone: "et opkald fra min mor" (a call from my mom).

et vidne.explanation: "Et vidne" means "a witness". To say you saw something happen, use "at være vidne til" (to witness): "Jeg var vidne til ulykken" (I witnessed the accident). A witness is a person, but "et bevis" (a piece of evidence) is a thing: "Billedet er et bevis" (The photo is evidence).

et vidnesbyrd.explanation: "Et vidnesbyrd" means "a testimony / evidence". To name what the evidence proves, use "om" (of): "et vidnesbyrd om hendes mod" (evidence of her courage). For what a person tells the police or a court, use "et vidneudsagn" (a witness statement): "Politiet har hørt hans vidneudsagn" (The police have heard his witness statement).

et vidneudsagn.explanation: "Et vidneudsagn" means "a testimony". It is built from "et vidne" (a witness) and "et udsagn" (a statement). To talk about what someone said, use "et udsagn" alone: "Hans udsagn var forkert" (His statement was wrong).

et vilkår.explanation: "Et vilkår" means "a term", as in an agreement. To tell someone to read the conditions of a contract: "Læs vilkårene først" (Read the terms first). When you talk about the circumstances someone works under, use it in the same way: "Det er svære vilkår at arbejde under" (These are difficult circumstances to work under).

et vindue.explanation: "Et vindue" means "a window". To talk about a window on a computer screen, the same word is used: "åbn et nyt vindue" (open a new window).

et vinglas.explanation: "Et vinglas" means "a wine glass". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "et glas" (a glass). The word "glas" is also the material: "en flaske af glas" (a bottle made of glass).

et visitkort.explanation: "Et visitkort" means "a business card". The part "kort" (card) is also in "et kreditkort" (a credit card): "Jeg betaler med kreditkort" (I pay with a credit card).
